2608.07222.title: Skaling: Chinchilla's Exponents Meet Kaplan's Coupling
2608.07222.paper_summary: Neural scaling laws are foundational for language model development, yet standard formulations systematically under- and overestimate loss at data-scarce and overtraining extremes. This failure originates in the underlying assumption that model size and training data impact the loss independently. To address this, we introduce the Skaling law, a generalized functional form that couples model capacity and data through a single interaction exponent. This simple extension reduces the Mean Absolute Percentage Error (MAPE) by 1.5-3x across both interpolation and extrapolation regimes. When paired with a sparse grid strategy restricted to low-compute regimes, the Skaling law achieves accurate full-grid extrapolation using approximately 10x less compute than uniform sweeps. By enabling reliable performance prediction from small-scale experiments, the Skaling law provides a more robust and resource-efficient framework for allocating compute budgets in next-generation model training.
2608.07222.paper_summary_zh: 神經縮放法則是語言模型開發的基礎，然而標準公式在數據稀缺和過度訓練的極端情況下系統性地低估和高估損失。這一失敗源於一個基本假設，即模型大小和訓練數據獨立影響損失。為了解決這個問題，我們引入了Skaling法則，一種通用的函數形式，通過單一的交互指數將模型容量和數據耦合起來。這一簡單的擴展在插值和外推範疇內將平均絕對百分比誤差（MAPE）降低了1.5-3倍。當與限制在低計算範疇內的稀疏網格策略結合時，Skaling法則能夠以大約10倍更少的計算量實現準確的全網格外推。通過使小規模實驗的性能預測更可靠，Skaling法則為下一代模型訓練中的計算預算分配提供了一個更穩健和資源高效的框架。
